subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). All five GR5 arms. ⛔ GR5 b/d resolve through FigurativeConstants.FillChar - the compiler's ONE definition of the alphanumeric high and low value, which 8.3.3.6.4 GR6 makes a PROGRAM-COLLATING-SEQUENCE-dependent fact rather than a constant - and NOT through a second map. This was measured wrong: PB151's landed ALLOCATE arm carried its own GR5 map spelling HIGH-VALUES as U+FFFF while every other HIGH-VALUE in the compiler is U+00FF under the native sequence. One rule, two places, two answers, and the arm with the private copy was the one that disagreed with the rest of the compiler. GR5 a is kept SEPARATE from GR5 d on purpose: 'a string of binary zeros' is the literal zero byte while 'the alphanumeric low value character' is the collating minimum - they coincide natively and diverge under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE. pb152_options_initialize_arm_agreement asks all three consuming arms the same HIGH-VALUES question in one program.
